subject: general
question: Nag Mk 2 Missile has been developed by which organisation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Defence Research and Development Organisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Nag Mk 2** is a **third-generation** **Anti-Tank Guided Missile (ATGM)** that has been indigenously designed and developed to strike enemy tanks with high precision.
 
• It is developed by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**, specifically through its premier lab, the **Defence Research and Development Laboratory (DRDL)**, located in **Hyderabad**.
 
• The missile is equipped with **Fire-and-Forget** capability, which means that once the missile is locked onto a target and launched, it guides itself automatically without further intervention from the operator.
 
• It uses an advanced **Imaging Infra-Red (IIR)** seeker to track and hit targets during both day and night, ensuring operational efficiency in diverse weather conditions.
 
• The development of the **Nag Mk 2** version focuses on enhanced performance, including improved seeker technology and a more efficient propulsion system compared to its predecessors. ***Hence, the correct answer is Defence Research and Development Organisation.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation):**
 
 
• Established in **1958**, it is the R&D wing of the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India.
 
• It aims to empower India with cutting-edge defense technologies and achieve self-reliance in critical military systems and platforms.
 
• It was formed by merging the **Technical Development Establishment (TDEs)** and the **Directorate of Technical Development & Production (DTDP)** with the **Defence Science Organisation (DSO)**.
 
 
 
• **Variants of Nag Missile:**
 
 
• **NAMICA (Nag Missile Carrier):** This is a modified **BMP-2** infantry combat vehicle designated as a "tank destroyer," equipped with a thermal sight and a launcher for **Nag** missiles.
 
• **Helina:** It is the helicopter-launched version of the Nag missile, boasting a range of **7 to 10 kilometers**. It is designed to be launched from the **HAL Rudra** and **Light Combat Helicopter (LCH)**.
 
• **Dhruvastra:** This is the Air Force version of the **Helina** missile, recently tested for integration with **Advanced Light Helicopters (ALH)**.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP):**
 
 
• The **Nag** missile was one of the five missile systems envisioned under the **IGMDP**, spearheaded by **Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam** in **1983**.
 
• The other four missiles under this program are **Prithvi** (Surface-to-surface), **Agni** (Ballistic missile), **Trishul** (Short-range surface-to-air), and **Akash** (Medium-range surface-to-air).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Operational Capabilities:** The **Nag** missile features a **top-attack capability**, allowing it to strike the turret of a tank, which is typically the most vulnerable part with the thinnest armor.
 
• **Range:** The land-based version has a minimum range of **500 meters** and an effective maximum range of up to **4 kilometers**.
 
• **Strategic Significance:** The successful induction of such indigenous systems strengthens India’s **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative in the **Defence Sector** and reduces dependency on foreign imports for anti-tank weaponry.
